diagnostic_bottleneck: Distinguishing Ergot elongated sclerotia from other panicle abnormalities (e.g., smut) without spore or honeydew evidence.

final_decision.reason: Dark, elongated horn‑like structures on the panicle correspond to Ergot's characteristic elongated sclerotia; other candidates lack panicle‑specific symptoms.

plant_part.specifics: Cylindrical seed head (panicle) densely packed with spherical grains (caryopses).

symptom_class.description: Presence of dark, elongated, horn-like structures interspersed among the normal white grains.

geometry.abnormal_structures: Elongated, conical or horn-like, tapering to a point.
geometry.orientation: Abnormal structures project outward from the panicle surface, often at an angle.

surface.abnormal_structures: Dark (black/dark grey), appearing hard or sclerotial, with a somewhat rough or textured surface.

texture.abnormal_structures: Hard, solid, distinct from the surrounding soft grain texture.

distribution.density: Moderate; abnormal structures are distributed along the length of the visible panicle section.

spatial_location.position: On the surface of the panicle, replacing or emerging from the position of individual grains.

reproductive_structure.details: Individual florets appear to be transformed into dark, elongated bodies rather than normal grains.

developmental_stage.details: Grains appear full-sized and white, suggesting the plant is in the late reproductive stage.

present: Structures projecting outward from the panicle
Structures occupying the position of individual grains
absent: Green ear transformation (panicle is not leafy)
uncertain: Internal structure of the dark bodies (sclerotium vs. smut ball)
Specific size comparison relative to a single grain (due to perspective)
